messages:
alex: quick check — I'm setting up a short-term sampling of request/response bodies in staging to investigate a parity bug. planning to capture full headers + body for 0.5% of traffic. is that okay or do we need redaction first? :thinking_face:
maria: prefer redact-first. bodies often contain emails/prompts/tokens. we require stripping auth tokens and PII before writing to any logs that could be viewed by engineers. staging still counts.
sam: fwiw the bug is in prompt truncation; seeing actual prompt examples will help. can we instead store a hashed prompt + a redacted snippet (first 100 chars) rather than full body?
maria: that'd be better. recommended pattern: store metadata + deterministic hash + redacted snippet. don't log any bearer tokens or cookie values.
ire ne: small nit — our fluentd pipeline currently supports sampling + transform. we can add a Lua filter to drop keys matching `/(password|token|authorization|cookie)/i` and then emit. sampling rate of 0.1% is our default for bodies; 0.5% is high but OK with approval.
alex: thanks. so action: change sampling to 0.1% by default, add hash+snippet approach. what about model prompts specifically — they sometimes include user PII in context. should we strip emails and phone numbers from snippets?
maria: yes. basic PII scrub (emails, phone numbers, national ids) is required. for prompts we should also remove long spans that look like logs or base64. regex examples: ```
// email
[emailRegex] = /[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/g
// phone (simple)
[phoneRegex] = /\b\d{3}[-\.\s]?\d{3}[-\.\s]?\d{4}\b/g
// token header
[tokenHeaderRegex] = /authorization:\s*bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9\-_.]+/i
```
maria: run those replacements before hashing/snippet. replace matches with `<REDACTED_EMAIL>` etc.
scott: (audit-bot) recorded policy reminder: any log containing PII must have ACLs and retention <= 30 days. create a ticket for exceptions.
alex: noted — i'll open a short JIRA and tag security. (link: https://jira.internal/redwood/INF-1234)
sam: one more question — headers: do we need to redact X-User-ID and X-Request-ID? request-id can stay; user-id should be hashed.
maria: yes, hash X-User-ID and drop any header that looks like an auth token. keep request-id for correlation.
irene: i'll put together the Fluentd filter PR with the regex and sampling param change. tagging @maria for review.
maria: sounds good. once PR is up, I'll do a quick review and confirm the Jira notes the retention + ACL requirement. :thumbsup:
audit-bot: action required: security approval needed for sampling >0.1% in staging. submit Jira flag for approval.
alex: thanks all — will keep this thread updated when PR/Jira links are posted.
